donorReadme: - Source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute/Lunar and Planetary Institute Color Maps of Iapetus - 2014 (PIA18436)
- Purpose: Cassini global color map for the explorable Iapetus moon pack

- Projection: equidistant/simple cylindrical global map, source feature coordinates are IAU planetographic positive-west, but the shipped texture is registered 180 degrees from the app's east-positive marker frame
- Processing: resized locally from the checked-in `11741x5871` source image to a true `4096x2048` JPEG sphere texture
- Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute/Lunar and Planetary Institute

coordinates.placement: latLonToXYZ in the donor src/entities/hotspot.ts, on Three.js SphereGeometry UVs
coordinates.longitudeDegrees: exactly as stored in features.json, placed by latLonToXYZ whatever the range; the donor stores values already in its own marker frame (see longitudeRange, markerLongitudeFromSource and donorReadmeNote)
coordinates.position: [radius * sin(phi) * sin(theta), radius * cos(phi), radius * sin(phi) * cos(theta)]
coordinates.donorReadmeNote: - The current Iapetus release uses the NASA/JPL PIA18436 Cassini global color map. Source coordinates in the USGS Gazetteer use Iapetus' IAU planetographic, positive-west, 0-360 system; because this texture is registered like the Tethys, Dione, and Rhea Cassini color maps, numeric marker longitudes use `markerLongitude = 180 - westLongitude`, normalized to `[-180, 180]`. Control checks: Turgis source `16.9 N, 28.4 W` maps to `151.6 E`; Carcassone Montes source `0.0 N, 216.7 W` maps to `36.7 W`; Toledo Montes source `0.0 N, 136.0 W` maps to `44.0 E`; Engelier and Gerin are visually calibrated near `42.4 S, 82 W` and `50 S, 54 W`.
